title: Determination 2023/010: Authority's decision to refuse a building consent for building work to enclose an existing carport
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Tasman District Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992). Fire-safety items reference the Acceptable Solution for C1-C6 Protection from Fire (C/AS2 firecell limits, escape distances). Edition not confirmed in the text read.

facts.text: The existing detached building (first built in 2006) is about 15.2 m long by 4.8 m wide. It has an office and a warehouse/despatch area, and an existing roller shutter or tilting door in one elevation.
An existing carport (about 4.9 m by 3.75 m, three open sides) attached to the building is to be enclosed on three sides with timber framing and plywood cladding to form a new garage.
The proposal also includes a 100 mm reinforced concrete floor slab, two roller shutter doors into the new garage, and fire exit signs above the two new roller shutter doors.
The consent application (BC211504) was supported by plans dated 1 December 2021. The determination records no other documentation for those plans, and the type of the existing door was not confirmed.

The ground floor plan (plan 201) shows purpose group WL, risk group WB, the firecell size, the number of escape routes and the escape path lengths, and states that fire-spread requirements do not change. The plans show two unlabelled escape routes.

The authority refused the consent application on 24 January 2022 on the basis of the original plans dated 1 December 2021. On 9 March 2022 the designer provided revised plans dated 27 January 2022 in response to the application for determination.
The parties give conflicting submissions on the intended use and whether there has been a change of use. The determination leaves change of use to the parties to resolve.

limitations: Regulator determination on a refusal for insufficient information. It makes no compliance finding on the fire design.
Change of use and the 2006 building's design are excluded from the determination (p.3 §1.7, §1.9).
Owner, designer and street address are omitted from the prompt.
Applies to the New Zealand Building Code only. No Alberta applicability is asserted.
